title: Readiness tab as tab 1 and the Overview-to-PRD rename
description: src/view/readiness.js lands and html-page.js wires it as the first tab. The former Overview tab becomes PRD (same panel content; the rename is label-only). The Readiness panel is the command page (DEFINE 2026-10-07, discovery-viewer-command-page): it renders the computeReadiness object as linked tables, counts and links, split into sub-tabs (Overview, Questions, Blocking, Coverage, Trace) whose key rides in the hash as sub=. Overview: tree line (formatTreeLine), two verdict cards at equal height (Ready for engineers, Ready to build; each count a link into the table it counts; chain term muted), a stage grid (D1 to D8 by tree and delta scope, pass/total per cell, failing count linked into the blocking table, acknowledged state with its reason from stages[].state), delta as counts with an on-demand per-document list, decisions outstanding in the #241 numbered format, and the freeze state in words (what blocks a freeze and what resolves it; no button, no command text). Questions: one table row per readiness.questions[] entry carrying number, the plain question, where it lives as a link, what settles it in plain words, a one-line copy handle (id plus ask, no command) and state; grouped by source span as a column. Blocking: one table row per failing item across every stage with stage, check, id as a resolving link (composite ids split on the first colon), the gate's why and what resolved looks like; no row cap; filterable by stage and persona. Coverage: a coverage summary with family counts, the three class totals as a stacked bar with the percentage, and an unresolved-pointers table, followed by the thin-requirements table fed by every signal that names a thin requirement (no story, zero criteria, criteria with no resolving test, D4 floor failures, no plain description). The For-engineers DocRow wrapper, the question cards, the blocker cards and the Freeze now control are retired; every engineer item survives in a named table or block (AC-18002-3). The profile register orders the first paint (product owner first unless the profile says engineer) and never hides a block (ADR-4127, ADR-4135). The view is pure: it never recomputes readiness, never renders a shell command and never writes, so the tab and rcf define readiness --json cannot disagree on the same tree hash. Every colour is an existing --sv-* token; the panel stays embed-safe under embed=1 and both themes.
rationale: Baz ruling 2026-09-22 (DEFINE step 2 spec section 2.4, decision 2): one object, two renderers. The CLI (REQ-175, PR B) and the tab (REQ-180, PR C) read the same computeReadiness result so they cannot disagree. Readiness is where an operator starts, so it must be tab 1. The Overview panel is just the PRD body today (phase 3.6 dropped the diagram) so the rename is honest; keeping the hash-anchor `#tab-overview` preserves every existing link into the surface. The L1 pre-population posture (ADR-4126) requires the tab to visibly distinguish [draft] shapes from settled ones, which the shapes:draftSettled check row makes legible.
